history.summary: HINDU Shaktism temple at Chottanikkara near Kochi, Ernakulam district, under the Cochin Devaswom Board (reportedly the most important of its 393 shrines across 3 districts). The presiding deity Rajarajeswari is worshipped in three forms across the day: Saraswati (white, morning), Lakshmi (crimson, noon) and Durga (blue, evening); an idol of Mahavishnu stands on the same pedestal, giving the names Amme Narayana / Devi Narayana. Legend says the deity was brought from Mookambika (Kollur) and that the temple was raised in a forest by Kannappan after the Goddess revealed herself through his calf. It is famed for healing mental illness and possession, and for the Guruthi ritual at the lower Kizhukkavu (Kizhakkavu) shrine. Temple architecture is noted for fine woodwork by vishwakarma sthapathis; entry through the west, with a Rakthakulam pond.

name: Chottanikkara Bhagavathy Temple
town_description: Chottanikkara is a town in Ernakulam district, about 17 km south of Kochi city, on the edge of the Kochi urban sprawl. It is one of Kerala's most visited pilgrim centres, drawing devotees year-round for the Bhagavathy temple and its healing rituals. The town sits in gently hilly terrain surrounded by fields and suburban development.
